newsitem.title: UK: Dollar sheds most gains after steep climb.
newsitem.headline: Dollar sheds most gains after steep climb.

text.p: The dollar lost most of the day's gains on Monday as traders pocketed profits from a steep climb triggered by helpful remarks from finance ministers of the G7 industrialised nations at the weekend.
European equity markets ended a lacklustre session with London and Paris making gains after trading that was dominated by upcoming general elections.

Most of the action was in currency markets. The dollar surged in early trade to a 37-month high against the mark and near its 55-month peak against the yen before easing in late trading as the bullish mood created by Sunday's G7 meeting cooled.
But traders said a pause for breath was only natural after the dollar's sprint forward.

"The outcome of this G7 meeting should be read as an indication that the G7 is still fairly content with a strong dollar though wary of overshooting in the future," said Joe Prendergast, currency strategist at Merrill Lynch in London.

In a communique after Sunday's meeting in Washington, the finance ministers said major currency misalignments had been corrected, and excessive volatility and deviations from fundamentals were undesirable.
The market was now likely to test central banks' resolve on intervention by bidding the dollar up gradually as fundamentals remain on the favourable side for the U.S. currency.
"The G7 meeting has left the foreign exchange market in the mood to test official resolve to maintain stable exchange rates," said Stephen Lewis, chief economist at London Bond Broking.

The dollar, which climbed one-and-a-half pfennigs in overnight deals, weakened to 1.7270 marks in late European trade, compared to 1.7235 on Friday. It was at 126.58 yen, off the day's peak of 127.10 .
A factor clouding the markets was a warning from the G7 ministers on trade imbalances.

They stressed the importance of avoiding currency moves that could lead to a re-emergence of large trade imbalances. They named no names, but markets saw this as a reference to Japan's swelling, politically sensitive trade surplus with the U.S.
But analysts agreed the authorities were likely to tolerate a rise in the dollar as long as it was slow, citing a comment made by Bank of England governor Eddie George after the meeting.
George said the G7 felt the currency environment was "in pretty good shape", and that no need had been expressed at the meeting for an action plan to deal with future currency moves.
Key focus for the dollar is the non-farm payrolls data on Friday. The currency is likely to be given a fillip if the jobs data is strong, analysts said.

In equity markets, French stocks made the healthiest gains, moving ahead to close up 0.55 percent with investors taking comfort from two polls giving the ruling centre-right coalition a sizeable majority in the upcoming parliamentary election.

A poll published in Monday's Le Figaro saw the centre-right winning the May 25-June 1 election with 329 seats, with the Socialists, other left and ecologists obtaining 202. Another poll published on Sunday also showed the RPR-UDF coalition and conservative allies winning.
The two polls provided some reassurance for the French financial markets, which were jolted last week by a poll predicting a tight race.
London shares, which barely moved for much of the day, spurted ahead in the last 30 minutes to close up 0.46 percent at 4389.7 points on the FTSE index as Wall Street recouped its initial losses.
The blue-chip index perked up after a weak opening and dull trade with sentiment subdued because of uncertainty over the outcome of the British election on Thursday.
"There is clearly no selling pressure," said one dealer. "We're creeping back to 4,400 again and when we're this close to the election that is very encouraging."

In Frankfurt, the picture was mixed with floor trade ending down 0.33 percent and deals on the computerised IBIS index making only modest gains, after getting an earlier boost from the stronger dollar and improved dollar prospects.
STOCKS
London's FTSE 100 closed up 20.0 points at 4,389.7.
The Paris CAC-40 index finished up 13.99 points at 2,550.25.
Frankfurt's DAX index ended down 14.21 points at 3363.06.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7270 against the mark versus 1.7235 in late European trade on Friday. Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 126.58 from 125.92.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was in the afternoon at $340.05 an ounce after ending at $342.45 in London on Friday. Silver was at $4.64, down nine points, in late trade. .
